title: Topology-aware partition guard and soft-capacity slots for predictable throughput
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools are occasionally experiencing unpredictable tail latency and throughput drops when colocated tenants (or bursty jobs) cause transient interference. Current hard-slicing approaches are too rigid for some workloads and lead to underutilized capacity. Goal: Implement a topology-aware Partition Guard that uses soft-capacity slots (elastic fractional reservations) plus a backpressure circuit to provide throughput guarantees while allowing efficient statistical multiplexing. The feature should integrate with autoscaling policies and quota enforcement so the system can gracefully degrade lower-priority tenants under contention rather than violating committed throughput SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Partition Guard schedules containers with awareness of GPU topology (NUMA nodes, NVLink domains) and avoids colocating high-interference tenants on the same domain when possible

Soft-capacity slots provide fractional reservation semantics (e.g., 0.25 GPU slot) with token-bucket accounting, and reclaim capacity during idle periods without violating reserved throughput contracts
Backpressure circuit detects noisy neighbor behavior (latency/SM utilization spikes) and applies per-tenant pacing or preemptive spill to burst pool within SLA rules
Autoscaling policy hooks trigger proactive scaling when effective capacity utilization for reserved slots exceeds 75% for 5 consecutive minutes, and scale-down follows a hysteresis rule
Quota enforcement includes soft and hard modes: soft triggers graceful degradation and throttling; hard rejects beyond-enforced limits with transparent error codes for customers

End-to-end experiment: for a mixed workload (20 tenants, 4 committed-throughput contracts), observed 95th percentile latency remains within 1.2x baseline under synthetic interference and total GPU utilization increases relative to hard-slicing by >= 12%
Monitoring dashboards display per-tenant reserved vs. used throughput, backpressure events, and autoscale actions; alerts created for repeated preemptions (>3 in 10m)
tasks: Design: define soft-slot semantics, token accounting, and topology constraints (Aisha)
Runtime: implement partition guard scheduler plugin with topology heuristics (Luca)
Billing/Quota: extend quota service to support fractional reservations and soft/hard enforcement (Rohit)
Autoscale: wire capacity metrics to autoscaler and implement proactive scale-up/scale-down policies (Megan)
Backpressure: implement circuit detector (latency + SM/PCIe metrics) and tenant pacing controller (Diego)
Integration tests: create mixed-tenancy scenarios and CI jobs that simulate noisy neighbors (QA)
Observability: add metrics, traces, and dashboard panels; define alerting rules (SRE)
Docs: write console and API docs for reserved slots, errors, and behavior under soft-preemption (Docs)
Rollout: staged canary in dedicated region eu-west-1 with opt-in customers, collect 2 weeks of telemetry
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha Moreno: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Primary risk is scheduler churn when many small fractional slots are active. Proposed mitigation: bucketize slot sizes and limit new allocations to 10/sec.
2025-02-18 - Luca Patel: PoC scheduler plugin implemented that reads GPU topology and applies a domain-avoidance heuristic. Need to add cost model for expected interference reduction.
2025-02-22 - Rohit Shah: Quota service schema extended to accept decimal reservations. Added migration plan for existing reservations to default to integer slots.
2025-02-25 - Diego Alvarez: Backpressure detector prototype triggered correctly on synthetic SM saturation; had two false positives during transient PCIe spikes — tuning thresholds next.
2025-03-01 - Megan Li: Autoscaler hook integrated; observed scale-ups on testbed at 80% reserved-slot saturation. Added 3-minute cooldown to avoid oscillation.
2025-03-02 - Design review (PM/Spike): PM requested clearer user-facing error codes when soft preemption happens. Action: Docs to map codes to recommended retry/backoff.
risks: Scheduler churn and allocation latency when handling many fractional reservations; could increase tail latency if not rate-limited
Migration complexity for existing Dedicated customers with hard slices — must preserve committed throughput or provide migration window
Risk of misclassification by backpressure detector leading to unnecessary throttling; requires conservative defaults and gradual rollout
Billing accuracy for fractional reservations must match telemetry; disputes possible if metrics drift
qa_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket accounting and fractional decrement/increment
Integration scenario: 10 tenants with mixed bursty and steady workloads; validate throughput SLAs under injected interference
Chaos test: randomly induce GPU noise (SM load/PCIe saturation) and verify graceful degradation and alerts
Performance test: compare utilization and 95th latency versus current hard-slicing baseline
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary on staging; validate metrics and rollback safety
Phase 2: Canary in eu-west-1 with two opt-in enterprise customers (week 1 monitoring)
Phase 3: Expand to all Dedicated fleets with default soft-mode off; enable by default after 4 weeks if no regressions
Rollback criteria: >3 customers report SLA violations OR repeated preemptions exceed threshold in production
notes: Follow-on work: expose per-tenant isolation level in Console UI and create a migration assistant for customers on hard slices
Consider bundling fractional slot pricing as optional add-on; collaborate with GTM for packaging
